title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Bootstrap inference provides confidence intervals indirect effects without assuming normality. medfit implements three bootstrap methods: Parametric bootstrap: Sample parameter distribution (fast, assumes normality) Nonparametric bootstrap: Resample data refit models (robust, slower) Plugin estimator: Point estimate (fastest, CI) methods return BootstrapResult object consistent structure.

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: examples use bundled, simulated mediation_demo data (see ?mediation_demo): randomized treatment, mediators mediator1 mediator2, outcome, two mediator-outcome confounders, covariate1 covariate2. Every model adjusts covariates.

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Samples estimated parameter distribution: Extract parameter estimates: \(\hat{\theta} = (\hat{}, \hat{b}, ...)\) Extract covariance matrix: \(\hat{\Sigma}\) Sample \(\theta^*_i \sim N(\hat{\theta}, \hat{\Sigma})\) Compute indirect effect: \(IE^*_i = ^*_i \times b^*_i\) Compute percentile CI bootstrap distribution Fast: model refitting required Appropriate : Parameters approximately normal (large n) Inappropriate : Small samples, non-normal parameters fast (refitting) Reproducible seed Works extracted models (need original data) Assumes multivariate normality parameters May underestimate uncertainty small samples
code: # Fit mediation models fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = mediation_demo) fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo)  # Extract mediation structure med_data <- extract_mediation(   fit_m,   model_y = fit_y,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1" )  # Define statistic function for indirect effect # Parameter names are prefixed by model: m_treatment (mediator model), # y_mediator1 and y_treatment (outcome model) indirect_effect <- function(theta) {   theta["m_treatment"] * theta["y_mediator1"] }  # Parametric bootstrap boot_result <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_effect,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_result) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   parametric Estimate:   0.3328 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.2170   Upper:   0.4631 summary(boot_result) Summary of BootstrapResult ==========================  Method:    parametric Estimate:  0.3327695 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower: 0.2170026   Upper: 0.4630625  Bootstrap Distribution Summary:    Min. 1st Qu. title: Bootstrap Inference
text: Resamples data refits models: Resample data replacement: \(D^*_i\) Refit mediator model \(D^*_i\) Refit outcome model \(D^*_i\) Extract paths: \(^*_i\), \(b^*_i\) Compute indirect effect: \(IE^*_i = ^*_i \times b^*_i\) Compute percentile CI bootstrap distribution Robust: Makes parametric assumptions Appropriate : Small samples, non-normal data, GLMs Gold standard: widely accepted method distributional assumptions Robust outliers Captures full sampling variability Computationally intensive (refits models B times) Requires original data Can slow complex models Speed parallel processing:
code: # Statistic function that refits models on resampled data statistic_fn_refit <- function(boot_data) {   # Fit models on bootstrap sample   fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,               data = boot_data)   fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,               data = boot_data)    # Extract and compute indirect effect   med_boot <- extract_mediation(fit_m, model_y = fit_y,                                 treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1")   med_boot@a_path * med_boot@b_path }  # Nonparametric bootstrap (requires original data) boot_np <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = statistic_fn_refit,   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123,   parallel = TRUE,   ncores = 4 )  print(boot_np) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.3328 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.2083   Upper:   0.4748 # Detect available cores ncores <- parallel::detectCores() - 1  # Run in parallel boot_np_par <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = statistic_fn_refit,   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 5000,   parallel = TRUE,   ncores = ncores,   seed = 123 )

code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)  nie_of <- function(d) {   fit <- fit_mediation(     Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = d, treatment = "X", mediator = "M",     engine = "lmer", cluster = "school"   )   unname(nie(fit)) }  boot_cl <- bootstrap_mediation(   nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",   n_boot = 200, ci_level = 0.95, seed = 123 ) Warning in .bootstrap_nonparametric_cluster(data, statistic_fn, n_boot, : 3 bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or non-convergent refits) boot_cl BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.2093 N bootstrap samples: 197  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:  -0.0038   Upper:   0.5241

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: serial mediation (treatment -> mediator1 -> mediator2 -> outcome), indirect effect product chain’s paths, \(\times d \times b\). parametric plugin methods accept SerialMediationData object (ParallelMediationData, InteractionMediationData, JointMediationData, ClusterMediationData) well MediationData. statistic_fn receives named @estimates vector, carries chain’s path aliases , d1, b, c_prime: lm chain estimates equation separately, covariance matrix sets covariances equations zero (see Model Extraction article). avoid assumption, bootstrap nonparametrically resampling data refitting three models:
code: # Fit the chain: each model adjusts for the covariates and every upstream # variable, so the outcome model includes mediator1 as well as mediator2 fit_serial <- function(d) {   extract_mediation(     lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d),     model_y = lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + mediator2 +                    covariate1 + covariate2, data = d),     treatment = "treatment",     mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),     mediator_models = list(       lm(mediator2 ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d)     )   ) } serial_med <- fit_serial(mediation_demo)  # Point estimate of the serial indirect effect (a * d * b) serial_med@a_path * serial_med@d_path * serial_med@b_path [1] 0.07545039 # Parametric bootstrap: draw the chain's paths from N(estimates, vcov) boot_serial_param <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = function(theta) unname(theta["a"] * theta["d1"] * theta["b"]),   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = serial_med,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_serial_param) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   parametric Estimate:   0.0755 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.0379   Upper:   0.1249 boot_serial <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = function(boot_data) {     s <- fit_serial(boot_data)     s@a_path * s@d_path * s@b_path   },   method = "nonparametric",   data = mediation_demo,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 123 )  print(boot_serial) BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.0755 N bootstrap samples: 1000  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:   0.0383   Upper:   0.1187

title: Bootstrap Inference
text: General guidelines: Exploratory: 1000 samples (fast) Publication: 5000+ samples (stable CI) High stakes: 10,000+ samples (stable) Check stability varying n_boot: CIs similar, n_boot sufficient.

title: medfit Cookbook
text: : treatment assigned whole clusters (schools) mediator outcome measured individuals. Formulas hold fixed effects ; engine adds random cluster intercept. clusters add se_type = "kr" (needs pbkrtest), bootstrap whole clusters product effects: warning, appears, counts draws dropped singular non-convergent refits; interval uses rest. spillover split large-cluster approximation, interval evidence cluster bootstrap designs; see Methods Formulas Bootstrap Inference.
code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n) xc <- fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat, treatment = "X",                     mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school") tidy(xc, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE) # A tibble: 5 × 5   term      estimate std_error conf_low conf_high   <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> 1 nie         0.209     0.127  -0.0397      0.458 2 nde         0.0772    0.227  -0.368       0.522 3 te          0.287     0.241  -0.186       0.760 4 own         0.103     0.0543 -0.00323     0.210 5 spillover   0.106     0.0886 -0.0675      0.280 decompose(xc) own spillover       nie 0.1032345 0.1061099 0.2093444 attr(,"label") [1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation" nie_of <- function(dd) {   unname(nie(fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = dd, treatment = "X",                            mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school"))) } boot_c <- bootstrap_mediation(   nie_of, method = "nonparametric", data = cdat, cluster = "school",   n_boot = 200, seed = 123 ) Warning in .bootstrap_nonparametric_cluster(data, statistic_fn, n_boot, : 3 bootstrap samples failed and were excluded (3 of them singular or non-convergent refits) boot_c BootstrapResult object ======================  Method:   nonparametric Estimate:   0.2093 N bootstrap samples: 197  95% Confidence Interval:   Lower:  -0.0038   Upper:   0.5241

code: set.seed(11) n <- 400 X <- rnorm(n) eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9) ldat <- data.frame(   X = X,   m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) ) ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) syntax <- "   eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3   eta ~ a * X   Y ~ b * eta + cp * X " xs <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",                     mediator = "eta", engine = "native") tidy(xs, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE) # A tibble: 3 × 5   term  estimate std_error conf_low conf_high   <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl> 1 nie      0.169    0.0310    0.108     0.229 2 nde      0.255    0.0487    0.159     0.350 3 te       0.423    0.0445    0.336     0.510 mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b") Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect  data:  a * b = 0 MBCO = 46.753, df = 1, p-value = 8.054e-12

code: base <- "   mediator1 ~ a * treatment   outcome ~ b * mediator1 + cp * treatment " free <- fit_sem(base, mediation_demo) tied <- fit_sem(paste0(base, "cp == a * b"), mediation_demo) rbind(free = coef(free)[c("a", "b", "cp")], tied = coef(tied)[c("a", "b", "cp")]) a         b         cp free 0.4559961 0.7134287 0.04057665 tied 0.3381172 0.6831633 0.23098930 chain <- "   mediator1 ~ a * treatment   mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + treatment   outcome ~ b * mediator2 + mediator1 + treatment " mbco_sem(fit_sem(chain, mediation_demo), paths = c("a", "d", "b")) Minimum-of-3 likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect  data:  a * d * b = 0 MBCO = 17.557, df = 1, p-value = 2.788e-05

what: 13. Joint significance for a binary or count outcome
title: medfit Cookbook
text: : outcome binary count want know whether mediated path exists, without outcome-scale effect. Test = 0 b = 0 separately take larger p-value (conservative). test likelihood-ratio test binomial Poisson model F test Gaussian, Gamma quasi* model, whose dispersion estimated. : GLM families.
code: d <- mediation_demo d$outcome_bin <- as.integer(d$outcome > median(d$outcome)) joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {   one <- function(fit, term) {     known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")     col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"     drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]   }   p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))   c(p, joint = max(p)) } fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d) fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,              data = d, family = binomial()) joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1") a            b        joint 8.096703e-09 2.024938e-12 8.096703e-09

title: Worked example: study hours, engagement and GPA
text: time spent studying raise GPA raises engagement course? Treatment \(X\): weekly study hours (hours). Mediator \(M\): course-engagement score (engagement). Outcome \(Y\): semester GPA (gpa). Covariates \(C\): prior GPA (prior_gpa) first-generation status (first_gen). two linear models \[ M = i_M + aX + \gamma_M^\top C + \varepsilon_M, \qquad Y = i_Y + bM + c'X + \gamma_Y^\top C + \varepsilon_Y . \] treatment--mediator interaction natural indirect effect \(\mathrm{NIE}=ab\), natural direct effect \(\mathrm{NDE}=c'\), total effect \(\mathrm{TE}=c'+ab\) per extra study hour. causal effects usual sequential-ignorability assumptions (section 9). sim_gpa() whole truth. coefficients analysis recover. code: mc <- function(n, reps, seed) {   set.seed(seed)   out <- matrix(NA_real_, reps, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, c("est", "se", "cover")))   for (r in seq_len(reps)) {     dd <- sim_gpa(n)     f <- fit_mediation(gpa ~ hours + engagement + prior_gpa + first_gen,                        engagement ~ hours + prior_gpa + first_gen,                        data = dd, treatment = "hours", mediator = "engagement")     e <- tidy(f, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)     e <- e[e$term == "nie", ]     out[r, ] <- c(e$estimate, e$std_error,                   e$conf_low <= truth[["nie"]] && truth[["nie"]] <= e$conf_high)   }   out } reps <- 400 mc500 <- mc(500, reps, seed = 1) mc100 <- mc(100, reps, seed = 2) summ <- function(m, n) {   c(n = n, reps = nrow(m), mean_est = mean(m[, "est"]),     bias = mean(m[, "est"]) - truth[["nie"]],     mc_se_bias = stats::sd(m[, "est"]) / sqrt(nrow(m)),     emp_sd = stats::sd(m[, "est"]), mean_se = mean(m[, "se"]),     coverage = mean(m[, "cover"])) } mc_table <- rbind(summ(mc500, 500), summ(mc100, 100)) round(mc_table, 4) n reps mean_est   bias mc_se_bias emp_sd mean_se coverage [1,] 500  400   0.0356 -4e-04      3e-04 0.0053  0.0050   0.9275 [2,] 100  400   0.0360  0e+00      6e-04 0.0111  0.0116   0.9650 chk("MC bias at n=500 within 3 MC se", mc_table[1, "bias"], 0, 3 * mc_table[1, "mc_se_bias"]) chk("MC mean delta se matches empirical sd at n=500 (10%, about 3 MC se)", mc_table[1, "mean_se"],     mc_table[1, "emp_sd"], 0.10 * mc_table[1, "emp_sd"]) chk("MC coverage at n=500 within 0.035 of 0.95 (3 MC se)", mc_table[1, "coverage"], 0.95, 0.035) chk("MC coverage at n=100 within 0.035 of 0.95 (3 MC se)", mc_table[2, "coverage"], 0.95, 0.035)

what: Extracting from lmer Models: Cluster-Level Treatment
title: Model Extraction
text: treatment assigned whole clusters (example schools) mediator outcome measured individuals (2-1-1 design), fit two linear mixed models lme4::lmer() pass extract_mediation(). returns ClusterMediationData object. outcome model must carry mediator within-cluster deviation plus observed cluster mean (raw mediator plus cluster mean); medfit finds terms value, grand-mean centering scale() work. natural indirect effect \(\, b_B\) (cluster-mean slope), decompose() splits -mediator part spillover part, labeled large-cluster approximation: fit_mediation(engine = "lmer", cluster = ) builds cluster means models , se_type = "kr" adds Kenward-Roger degrees freedom (needs pbkrtest). -cluster warnings, assumptions effect needs formulas Methods Formulas; use bootstrap_mediation(cluster = ) intervals products (Bootstrap).
code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) cdat$M_bar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$M_w <- cdat$M - cdat$M_bar cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * cdat$M_w + 0.6 * cdat$M_bar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n)  fit_m <- lme4::lmer(M ~ X + (1 | school), data = cdat) fit_y <- lme4::lmer(Y ~ X + M_w + M_bar + (1 | school), data = cdat) cluster_med <- extract_mediation(   fit_m, model_y = fit_y, treatment = "X", mediator = "M", cluster = "school" ) cluster_med <ClusterMediationData>   X -> M -> Y  (clusters: school)   a = +0.2720   b_within = +0.3796   b_between = +0.7697   c' = +0.0772   NIE (a * b_between) = +0.2093   n = 400 in 40 clusters (sizes 10 to 10)   |   within outcome model, model SEs Estimand and assumptions:   Design: treatment `X` assigned to 40 clusters (`school`, sizes 10 to 10); linear     mixed models with a random cluster intercept, mediator entering through the     observed cluster mean.   - All rows: linear models with no mediator-by-treatment or mediator-by-covariate     products; treatment randomized; clusters intact.   - Own (a * b_within): no unmeasured lower-level M-Y confounding; additive upper-level     confounders are allowed because level-1 covariates are cluster-mean centered.   - Spillover, NIE and NDE: also no unmeasured upper-level M-Y confounding.   - TE: no assumption beyond randomization of the treatment.   - Own/spillover split: a cross-world assumption across individuals in a cluster; no     treatment-induced M-Y confounding.   - Interference only through the observed cluster mean of the mediator and none     between clusters; members missing from the analysis rows are assumed not to drive     their peers' outcomes. nie(cluster_med) Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.2093 decompose(cluster_med) own spillover       nie 0.1032345 0.1061099 0.2093444 attr(,"label") [1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation"

title: Model Extraction
text: treatment mediator interact, total effect splits four pieces (VanderWeele 2014): controlled direct effect (CDE), reference interaction (INTref), mediated interaction (INTmed), pure indirect effect (PIE), Total = CDE + INTref + INTmed + PIE, NDE = CDE + INTref, NIE = INTmed + PIE. medfit computes decomposition; causal interpretation (requires VanderWeele’s -unmeasured-confounding assumptions) analyst’s responsibility. extract_mediation() returns InteractionMediationData object whenever outcome model carries X:M term. Set reference mediator level m_star (default 0). lm/glm, X:M term detected automatically. mediation_demo’s outcome_int carries treatment mediator1 interaction: tidy() reports four components type = "components" natural effects type = "effects"; glance() adds interaction coefficient m_star: four-way formulas (continuous Y M) CDE = θ₁ + θ₃·m*, INTref = θ₃·(E[M|X=0] − m*), INTmed = θ₃·β₁, PIE = θ₂·β₁, θ₃ interaction coefficient β₁ path. decomposition needs Gaussian mediator outcome models identity link. non-Gaussian family stops informative error, non-identity link stops Four-way decomposition requires identity link. lavaan interaction enters product variable (column create), model must fit meanstructure = TRUE mediator intercept (needed INTref) estimated. Name product term via interaction: interaction absent (decomposition = "two_way"), extraction falls back standard MediationData — existing two-way workflows unchanged. two paths extract models fit. fit_mediation() can instead delegate fitting regmedint package, implements VanderWeele’s regression-based estimators closed form, hand back medfit classes: return class follows rule extract_mediation(): X:M term formula_y yields InteractionMediationData, absence plain MediationData. Components map regmedint’s output CDE = cde, INTref = pnde − cde, INTmed = tnie − pnie, PIE = pnie. Standard errors come regmedint’s delta method rather medfit’s, analytical — bootstrap needed — reproduce SEs regmedint::summary() reports model. four-way split read reference mediator level \(m^*\): \[\text{CDE} = \theta_1 + \theta_3 m^*\] \[\text{INTref} = \theta_3\,(E[M \mid X = 0] - m^*)\] Set fit_mediation(m_star = ), defaults 0 every engine: two terms shift exactly compensating directions, nde(), nie(), te(), pm() invariant m_star — CDE/INTref split moves. Passing m_star fit treatment--mediator term error, silent -op. engines reach answer different routes. engine = "glm" applies m_star extraction time, coefficients fit; engine = "regmedint" hands value regmedint::regmedint() m_cde argument, closed-form estimator consumes fitting time. two names denote one quantity, m_cde accepted engine_args — use m_star. Everything regmedint-specific reference level goes engine_args: Recognized names interaction, cvar, mreg, yreg, a0, a1, c_cond; replaces value adapter otherwise derive formulas, families, data. Scope. regmedint engine needs numeric 0/1 treatment linear (Gaussian) mediator model; outcome may Gaussian binomial. Outside range regmedint’s closed-form effects stop products regression coefficients MediationData InteractionMediationData defined terms , adapter raises explicit error instead returning object whose numbers disagree nie(). weights se_type = "sandwich" likewise refused rather silently ignored. regmedint suggested package — install install.packages("regmedint").

reference mediator level for the decomposition )  decompose(med_int)                          # CDE, INTref, INTmed, PIE + effects cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total 0.21521278 0.04353909 0.27709549 0.34001758 0.25875187 0.61711307 0.87586495 confint(med_int, parm = "components")       # delta-method CIs for the components Normal (delta-method) approximation for four-way components; consider bootstrap_mediation() for robust inference. 2.5 %    97.5 % cde     -0.01242752 0.4428531 int_ref -0.02378409 0.1108623 int_med  0.13266955 0.4215214 pie      0.19952257 0.4805126 library(generics) tidy(med_int, type = "components", conf_int = TRUE) # title: Model Extraction
text: fit_sem() fits model syntax native engine returns SEMFit. extract_mediation() accepts arguments lavaan method returns classes: treatment--mediator product outcome equation gives four-way decomposition route. Write model syntax treatment:mediator1 (colon, spaces); engine builds column, turns mean structure , stores term canonical name mediator1:treatment, whichever order write : Without product, decomposition = "four_way" interaction = refused name, message says add product. precomputed product column fitted ordinary variable, write product syntax. model product must stay inside supported class (see native model page), global chi-square NA product factor regression target. See ?"medfit-syntax" syntax.
code: sem <- fit_sem(   "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nab := a*b",   data = mediation_demo ) x_sem <- extract_mediation(sem, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1") nie(x_sem) Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.3253 sem4 <- suppressWarnings(fit_sem(   "mediator1 ~ treatment    outcome_int ~ treatment + mediator1 + treatment:mediator1",   data = mediation_demo, se_type = "sandwich" )) x4 <- extract_mediation(sem4, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",                         outcome = "outcome_int") class(x4)[1] [1] "medfit::InteractionMediationData" decompose(x4) cde    int_ref    int_med        pie        nde        nie      total 0.04048833 0.07763088 0.22810575 0.32526471 0.11811921 0.55337046 0.67148967

text: estimates property contains parameters models: Use covariance matrix computing standard errors:
code: med_data <- extract_mediation(model_m, model_y, treatment = "treatment",                               mediator = "mediator1")  # All parameters (intercepts + coefficients) med_data@estimates m_(Intercept)   m_treatment  m_covariate1  m_covariate2 y_(Intercept)    0.02052158    0.58264246    0.44789496    0.13109906    0.17120346   y_treatment   y_mediator1  y_covariate1  y_covariate2             a    0.20579826    0.57113843    0.35665236    0.05259769    0.58264246             b       c_prime    0.57113843    0.20579826 # Access by name med_data@estimates["a"]  # a_path a 0.5826425 med_data@estimates["b"]  # b_path b 0.5711384 # Covariance matrix of all parameters vcov_mat <- med_data@vcov  # For delta method SE of indirect effect (a*b): # Var(ab) = b^2 * Var(a) + a^2 * Var(b) + 2ab*Cov(a,b)  a <- med_data@a_path b <- med_data@b_path var_a <- vcov_mat["a", "a"] var_b <- vcov_mat["b", "b"] cov_ab <- vcov_mat["a", "b"]  var_indirect <- b^2 * var_a + a^2 * var_b + 2 * a * b * cov_ab se_indirect <- sqrt(var_indirect)  se_indirect [1] 0.06449767

title: Introduction to medfit
text: medfit provides unified infrastructure mediation analysis R. offers: Short entry points: med() quick analysis, quick() instant results Effect extractors: nie(), nde(), te(), pm(), paths() mediation effects Tidyverse integration: tidy() glance() methods tibble workflows Base R generics: coef(), vcov(), confint(), nobs() S7 classes Native SEM engine: fit_sem() fits model syntax latent mediators linear nonlinear constraints; mbco_sem() tests indirect effect, anova() compares nested fits, tidy(), glance() confint() summarize SEMFit; observed intercepts means (y ~ 1), fixed_x x:m product term (four-way decomposition extract_mediation()) supported inside documented limits S7-based classes standardized mediation data structures Foundation mediation analysis ecosystem (RMediation, mediationverse) package eliminates code duplication across mediation packages providing shared infrastructure allowing package focus unique methodological contributions.

title: Introduction to medfit
text: medfit defines S7 classes mediation structure: MediationData (simple), InteractionMediationData (simple treatment--mediator interaction), SerialMediationData, ParallelMediationData, JointMediationData (several mediators treatment--mediator products), ClusterMediationData (treatment assigned whole clusters, lmer fits), BootstrapResult. eighth class, SEMFit, holds model fitted syntax native engine (fit_sem()). three common classes introduced ; see Model Extraction others. Stores simple mediation models (X -> M -> Y): indirect effect computed * b. Use effect extractors: Stores serial mediation models (X -> M1 -> M2 -> … -> Y): two mediators, serial indirect effect * d * b: Design extensibility: 3+ mediators, d_path becomes vector: - 3 mediators: * d21 * d32 * b (product--four) - k mediators: product--(k+1) Stores bootstrap inference results:

text: simplest way run mediation analysis: Dedicated functions extracting mediation effects: Extract mediation structure pre-fitted models: See Model Extraction details. Fit mediation models formula interface: Fit model written syntax native maximum-likelihood engine. handles latent variables constraints, := defines effect delta-method standard error: See ?"medfit-syntax" syntax Cookbook latent-mediator example. Perform bootstrap inference indirect effects: See Bootstrap Inference details.
code: library(medfit)  # mediation_demo: simulated data bundled with medfit (see ?mediation_demo). # Its covariates confound the mediator-outcome relation, so adjust for them. result <- med(   data = mediation_demo,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1",   outcome = "outcome",   covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2") )  # Instant summary quick(result) NIE = 0.333  | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 % # With bootstrap CI result_boot <- med(   data = mediation_demo,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1",   outcome = "outcome",   covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2"),   boot = TRUE,   n_boot = 1000,   seed = 42 )  quick(result_boot) NIE = 0.333  [0.21, 0.464] | NDE = 0.206 | PM = 61.8 % nie(result)   # Natural Indirect Effect (a * b) Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.3328 nde(result)   # Natural Direct Effect (c') Natural Direct Effect (NDE): 0.2058 te(result)    # Total Effect (nie + nde) Total Effect (TE): 0.5386 pm(result)    # Proportion Mediated Proportion Mediated (PM): 0.6179 paths(result) # All path coefficients (a, b, c') a         b   c_prime 0.5826425 0.5711384 0.2057983 # From lm/glm models fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo) fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,             data = mediation_demo)  med_data <- extract_mediation(   fit_m,   model_y = fit_y,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1" )  # From a fitted lavaan SEM model (paths labeled a, b, cp) sem_model <- "   mediator1 ~ a * treatment + covariate1 + covariate2   outcome ~ cp * treatment + b * mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2 " lavaan_fit <- lavaan::sem(sem_model, data = mediation_demo) med_data <- extract_mediation(   lavaan_fit,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1",   outcome = "outcome" ) # Fit using GLM engine med_data <- fit_mediation(   formula_y = outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,   formula_m = mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,   data = mediation_demo,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1" ) sem <- fit_sem(   "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nab := a*b",   data = mediation_demo ) sem@defined name expr       est         se 1   ab  a*b 0.3253207 0.08016376 # Define statistic function indirect_fn <- function(theta) {   theta["m_treatment"] * theta["y_mediator1"] }  # Parametric bootstrap boot_result <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_fn,   method = "parametric",   mediation_data = med_data,   n_boot = 1000,   ci_level = 0.95,   seed = 12345 )  # title: Cluster-randomized trials (2-1-1)
text: data simulated: 40 schools 10 students, treatment assigned school. formulas hold fixed effects ; engine adds random cluster intercept cluster-mean within-cluster terms mediator. path b_between effect cluster’s mean mediator outcome, b_within effect individual’s deviation cluster mean. indirect effect uses -cluster path, treatment moves whole clusters.
code: set.seed(2026) J <- 40 n <- 10 cl <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) x_j <- sample(rep(0:1, length.out = J)) v <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) u <- rnorm(J, sd = 0.5) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(cl), X = x_j[cl]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + v[cl] + rnorm(J * n) mbar <- ave(cdat$M, cdat$school) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.3 * (cdat$M - mbar) + 0.6 * mbar + u[cl] + rnorm(J * n) x <- fit_mediation(Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat, treatment = "X",                    mediator = "M", engine = "lmer", cluster = "school") class(x)[1] [1] "medfit::ClusterMediationData" paths(x) a   b_within  b_between    c_prime 0.27198520 0.37955931 0.76969028 0.07722813

code: joint_test <- function(fit_a, term_a, fit_b, term_b) {   one <- function(fit, term) {     known <- fit$family$family %in% c("binomial", "poisson")     col <- if (known) "Pr(>Chi)" else "Pr(>F)"     drop1(fit, scope = term, test = if (known) "LRT" else "F")[term, col]   }   p <- c(a = one(fit_a, term_a), b = one(fit_b, term_b))   c(p, joint = max(p)) } fit_a <- glm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = d) fit_b <- glm(outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,              data = d, family = binomial()) joint_test(fit_a, "treatment", fit_b, "mediator1") a            b        joint 8.096703e-09 2.024938e-12 8.096703e-09

Comparing software 1e-6 means first checking one actually converged.
code: # The simple mediation model in semopy, for the syntax crosswalk article (vignettes/articles/syntax-crosswalk.qmd). # Run from the package root: #   Rscript -e 'write.csv(medfit::mediation_demo, "mediation_demo.csv", row.names = FALSE)' #   uv run --with semopy==2.3.11 python -I tests/sim/oracles/semopy-simple.py mediation_demo.csv \ #     > tests/sim/oracles/semopy-simple.csv # semopy's default SLSQP stop leaves the estimates about 4e-5 from the optimum; ftol = 1e-12 removes that. import sys  import pandas as pd import semopy  data = pd.read_csv(sys.argv[1]) model = semopy.Model(""" mediator1 ~ a*treatment outcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment """) model.fit(data, obj="MLW", options={"ftol": 1e-12}) out = model.inspect()[["lval", "op", "rval", "Estimate", "Std. Err"]] out.columns = ["lhs", "op", "rhs", "estimate", "std_error"] out.insert(0, "semopy", semopy.__version__) out.to_csv(sys.stdout, index=False, float_format="%.12g") semopy <- read.csv(file.path(oracles, "semopy-simple.csv")) labels <- c("mediator1~treatment" = "a", "outcome~mediator1" = "b", "outcome~treatment" = "cp") key <- paste0(semopy$lhs, semopy$op, semopy$rhs) semopy$term <- ifelse(key %in% names(labels), labels[key], key) stopifnot(nrow(semopy) == 5) fixed <- tidy(fit_sem(model, mediation_demo)) both <- merge(semopy[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")],               fixed[, c("term", "estimate", "std_error")], by = "term",               suffixes = c("_semopy", "_medfit")) both term estimate_semopy std_error_semopy estimate_medfit 1                    a      0.45599616       0.10763362      0.45599612 2                    b      0.71342892       0.05047200      0.71342873 3                   cp      0.04057561       0.11106055      0.04057665 4 mediator1~~mediator1      1.15847060       0.08191624      1.15847022 5     outcome~~outcome      1.18044581       0.08347012      1.18044625   std_error_medfit 1       0.10763360 2       0.05047202 3       0.11106057 4       0.08191621 5       0.08347015 stopifnot(max(abs(both$estimate_semopy - both$estimate_medfit)) < 1e-5,           max(abs(both$std_error_semopy - both$std_error_medfit)) < 1e-5)

code: # 40 schools of 10 students, treatment assigned by school set.seed(123) J <- 40 n <- 10 school <- rep(seq_len(J), each = n) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(school), X = sample(rep(0:1, J / 2))[school]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[school] + rnorm(J * n) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.4 * cdat$M + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[school] + rnorm(J * n)  fit <- fit_mediation(   Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat,   treatment = "X", mediator = "M",   engine = "lmer", cluster = "school" )  nie(fit)        # a * b_between decompose(fit)  # own-mediator and spillover parts (large-cluster approximation) #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.328 #>        own  spillover        nie #> 0.25763321 0.07036432 0.32799753 # a latent mediator `eta` with three indicators, simulated set.seed(11) n <- 400 X <- rnorm(n) eta <- 0.5 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.9) ldat <- data.frame(   X = X,   m1 = eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m2 = 0.8 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.7),   m3 = 0.7 * eta + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8) ) ldat$Y <- 0.4 * eta + 0.2 * X + rnorm(n, sd = 0.8)  syntax <- "   eta =~ m1 + m2 + m3   eta ~ a * X   Y ~ b * eta + cp * X " fit <- fit_mediation(model = syntax, data = ldat, treatment = "X",                      mediator = "eta", engine = "native") nie(fit)  mbco_sem(fit_sem(syntax, ldat), "a", "b")  # minimum of two likelihood-ratio tests #> Natural Indirect Effect (NIE): 0.1685 #> #>  Minimum-of-two likelihood-ratio tests (MBCO) for an indirect effect #> #> data:  a * b = 0 #> MBCO = 46.753, df = 1, p-value = 8.054e-12

Define indirect effect function indirect_fn <- function(theta) theta["m_treatment"] * theta["y_mediator1"]  # Plugin estimator (point estimate only, fastest) result_plugin <- bootstrap_mediation(   statistic_fn = indirect_fn,   method = "plugin",   mediation_data = med_data ) print(result_plugin) #> BootstrapResult object #> ====================== #>  #> Method:   plugin #> Estimate:   0.3328 #>  #> (No confidence interval for plugin method)  # code: # mediation_demo is simulated data bundled with medfit; its covariates # confound the mediator-outcome relation, so both models adjust for them med_data <- fit_mediation(   formula_y = outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,   formula_m = mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,   data = mediation_demo,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1" ) print(med_data) #> MediationData object #> ==================== #>  #> Path coefficients: #>   a (X -> M):        0.5826 #>   b (M -> Y|X):      0.5711 #>   c' (X -> Y|M):     0.2058 #>   Indirect (a*b):    0.3328 #>  #> Variables: #>   Treatment: treatment #>   Mediator:  mediator1 #>   Outcome:   outcome #>  #> Model info: #>   N observations: 400 #>   Converged:      Yes #>   Source:         stats::glm #>  #> Residual SDs: #>   Mediator model:   0.9792 #>   Outcome model:    1.0426  # \donttest{ # Binary outcome (takes longer to fit): dichotomize the outcome at its median demo <- mediation_demo demo$outcome_bin <- as.integer(demo$outcome > stats::median(demo$outcome)) med_data_bin <- fit_mediation(   formula_y = outcome_bin ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,   formula_m = mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,   data = demo,   treatment = "treatment",   mediator = "mediator1",   family_y = binomial() ) # }  # \donttest{ if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) { # Treatment assigned to whole clusters (needs lme4); formulas hold fixed # effects only, the engine adds the random cluster intercept set.seed(1) J <- 30 id <- rep(seq_len(J), each = 6) cdat <- data.frame(school = factor(id), X = sample(rep(0:1, J / 2))[id]) cdat$M <- 0.5 * cdat$X + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[id] + rnorm(J * 6) cdat$Y <- 0.2 * cdat$X + 0.4 * cdat$M + rnorm(J, sd = 0.5)[id] + rnorm(J * 6) cluster_fit <- fit_mediation(   Y ~ X + M, M ~ X, data = cdat,   treatment = "X", mediator = "M",   engine = "lmer", cluster = "school" ) nie(cluster_fit)       # a * b_between decompose(cluster_fit) # own-mediator and spillover parts } #>        own  spillover        nie  #> 0.26012673 0.03260194 0.29272868  #> attr(,"label") #> [1] "cluster-average, large-cluster approximation" # }
